findings.symptom: Login and every write request hung indefinitely; the live feed had been stalled for 7 h 40 min with 14 database sessions queued.
findings.cause: When the PC slept, a database session whose client had gone away kept the row lock on the workspace-state row. Nothing timed out: TCP keepalive was the 2-hour system default, lock waits were unlimited, and the API and worker had no handler for a lost database connection (they either hung or, once detected, crashed and stayed down).
findings.fix: backend/src/database.mjs (+ live-voice.mjs): connections use TCP keepalive (dead peers detected in about a minute), a 45 s lock timeout, and connection-loss events are handled instead of terminating the process. Proven by terminating all 14 application database sessions: API and worker kept the same process ids and served the next request.

findings.symptom: New meetings never appeared: the page showed the 200 oldest of 3,230 meetings.
findings.cause: The list query ordered by start time ascending with LIMIT 200.
findings.fix: backend/src/agent-orchestrator.mjs: return the latest 200 meetings, still in chronological order.

findings.symptom: Totals showed 200 open / 0 completed while the database held 11,359 open and 851 completed.
findings.cause: Statistics were computed from the 200-row page instead of the whole queue.
findings.fix: backend/src/agent-orchestrator.mjs + index.mjs: totals now come from a database aggregate over the full queue.

findings.feature: Live Sync, Overview activity, Data Hub
findings.symptom: The 'recent events' stream was about 9 hours stale and missed new events.
findings.cause: Events are loaded newest-first but the code sliced the tail of the list, i.e. the oldest entries; the in-memory buffer mixed both orders after a restart.
findings.fix: backend/src/index.mjs: keep the in-memory buffer oldest-to-newest and take the newest 50 for the stream.

findings.symptom: Cohort report was always empty (0 acquired, 0 conversions, 0 revenue) despite 2,400 attributed purchases; Planner had no revenue evidence.
findings.cause: Attribution tables enforce row-level security, but the cohort queries ran without the tenant database context and therefore read zero rows.
findings.fix: backend/src/cohort-analytics.mjs: run both queries inside the tenant transaction context.

findings.symptom: A privacy export for a customer with visits, purchases and a lead profile returned none of them; a deletion request would have left that data in place.
findings.cause: Same missing tenant context for the attribution tables, and the customer/visitor selector never matched lead profiles because they are keyed by the customer id.
findings.fix: backend/src/privacy-ops.mjs: export, delete and retention purge run in the tenant context; customer and visitor selectors also match the lead profile id.

findings.symptom: 5,668 ML scoring jobs were dead-lettered with 'artifact metadata not found', and the feed never recovered.
findings.cause: The feed kept scoring against saved model artifacts that no longer existed and never retrained.
findings.fix: scripts/live/generator.mjs and ace_feed.py: a scoring job that fails drops its artifact so the next AI cycle retrains.

findings.symptom: Every signed-in API call took 2.5–4.5 s (GET /auth/me 4.3 s; Boards stayed on "Loading"), against 0.25 s for the unauthenticated health check.
findings.cause: Each request downloaded and re-parsed the entire workspace-state row, which had grown to 23 MB of JSON.
findings.fix: backend/src/store.mjs: the parsed state is reused while the row version is unchanged (a cheap version query per request; writers in any process bump the version). GET /auth/me now 0.5 s, GET /boards 0.26 s; feed median request time 569 ms → 228 ms.

findings.symptom: After a phone call, a lead acquired from Google or Meta showed "call" as its first-touch source.
findings.cause: The call webhook overwrote the stored acquisition source and campaign on the existing lead profile.
findings.fix: backend/src/lead-ops.mjs + index.mjs: call events keep an existing lead's acquisition source and campaign; they only set them for a lead first seen through the call.

findings.cause: The API returned the raw database average.
findings.fix: backend/src/lead-ops.mjs: average score is rounded to one decimal (65.1).

findings.feature: AI Intelligence (page load) and every page that loads several panels
findings.symptom: AI Intelligence stayed on "Loading AI intelligence" for 12 seconds; 20 simultaneous requests took 5.7 s even for the cheapest endpoint.
findings.cause: Each request still made a full private copy of the 23 MB workspace state on the single server thread, so parallel requests queued behind one another.
findings.fix: backend/src/store.mjs: a request now copies only the parts of the state it reads. 20 simultaneous requests: 5.7 s → 14 ms; AI Intelligence loads in 0.8 s; feed median request time 265 ms → 12 ms. Writes stay consistent with the database (verified after each write).

findings.symptom: 0 active routes, 0 qualified evaluations, 0 datasets: trained local models could never become active.
findings.cause: No evaluation policy existed, nothing was ever qualified, approved or deployed, and deployment of local models was blocked by a hard-coded "capability not verified" flag.
findings.fix: The feed now runs the governed lifecycle (point-in-time dataset → train → qualify against a predeclared policy → approve → deploy). The capability flag is now an explicit opt-in, AI_LOCAL_ML_CAPABILITY_VERIFIED, enabled only in this local stack. Result: 6 active routes, 6 qualified evaluations, datasets listed.

findings.symptom: Chronos forecasting was unavailable, and once installed every forecast failed with "Cannot change data-type for array of references".
findings.cause: The optional package and checkpoint were not provisioned; the pipeline also passed timezone-aware timestamps, which the Chronos library cannot process (the code path had never run).
findings.fix: Installed chronos-forecasting with CPU PyTorch, provisioned the pinned amazon/chronos-2 snapshot, and ml-service/src/acemarketing_ml/pipelines.py now normalises timestamps to naive UTC. Forecast job succeeds in about 27 s on CPU.

findings.cause: Optional econml package was not installed.
findings.fix: Installed econml 0.17 with the core ML stack pinned unchanged; the feed submits a confounded remarketing-exposure dataset and the job completes.

findings.symptom: The open queue only grew (12,212 open) and the page, which lists the 200 most overdue, never showed anything new.
findings.cause: Every lead creates follow-ups automatically but the feed completed far fewer than were created.
findings.fix: scripts/live/ace_feed.py: each cycle the feed completes the most overdue tasks, faster while the backlog is large. The backlog is now shrinking.

findings.symptom: Every state-changing request took 1.5–3 s; one tracking event took up to 4.4 s.
findings.cause: PostgreSQL spent about 3 s recompressing the 24 MB workspace-state row with the default pglz compression on each write.
findings.fix: backend/migrations/061_workspace_state_lz4.sql: the column now uses lz4 compression (rewrite 3.0 s → 0.66 s on a copy). Call webhook 1.5 s → 0.6 s; personalization decision 1.8 s → 0.9 s.

findings.symptom: "Run governed analysis" was blocked ("AI task is not active"), and once a job did succeed the answer was never shown on the Analyst tab.
findings.cause: The analyst route only supported OpenAI's API; no code path could produce the qualified evaluation a hosted model needs to become active; and the page tracked the job status but never fetched or rendered its result.
findings.fix: Added an NVIDIA (OpenAI-compatible) analyst provider with access verification and retry on 429/503, a five-case grounding evaluation endpoint, and an answer panel on the Analyst tab. nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b scored 5/5 (cites evidence, recalls figures, declines unanswerable questions) and is deployed; answers appear in about a minute.

openItems.area: Funnel, Journeys, Customer 360, Behavior, Match Quality
openItems.observation: These pages calculate from a recent window (latest 500 lead profiles or 5,000 events), not the whole workspace. Funnel reports 500 leads while 10,000+ exist.
openItems.recommendation: Move these totals to database aggregates, as was done for Lead Grading and now Follow-ups. This touches 18 call sites, so it was not changed in this run.

openItems.observation: http://localhost:5173 on this PC opens a different project ("Apex CRM"): another Vite server owns the IPv6 localhost:5173 listener.
openItems.recommendation: Open AceMarketing at http://127.0.0.1:5173, or stop the other dev server.

openItems.observation: With AUTH_REQUIRED unset, the API serves reads without a token and accepts any password for the owner account. This is by design for local development.
openItems.recommendation: Set AUTH_REQUIRED=true (or run in production mode) before the stack is reachable by anyone else.

openItems.observation: A customer who messages on WhatsApp gets a second lead profile keyed by phone number (source "WhatsApp") instead of being merged into their existing profile with the same phone hash.
openItems.recommendation: Stitch WhatsApp senders to an existing profile by phone hash before creating a new one.

openItems.observation: 3 of 208 backend foundation tests fail on this PC, with or without today's changes: control idempotency (2) and secure object lifecycle (1). The in-memory test database does not honour the ON CONFLICT unique key that real PostgreSQL enforces.
openItems.recommendation: Run these three against PostgreSQL, or pin the pg-mem version they last passed with.

openItems.observation: Records created by earlier feed versions remain: 4,711 A-grade leads, names ending in "(test)", and about 11,000 open follow-ups. The Python feed now completes the most overdue follow-ups each cycle.
openItems.recommendation: Reset the local test database if a clean baseline is wanted.

openItems.observation: 7 routes stay blocked: recommendation reviewer, multimodal extraction, embeddings, reranking, call transcription, live voice and creative image (Anthropic, Google, Voyage). Knowledge sources therefore stay at "pending_embedding" and activation proposals cannot be reviewed. The analyst sends about 350 KB of evidence per question, which makes each answer take about a minute.
openItems.recommendation: Add those provider keys, or route more text tasks to the NVIDIA endpoint; trim the analyst evidence snapshot to speed answers up.

openItems.observation: google-meridian 2.1.0 requires numpy below 2.4; the working ML stack runs numpy 2.5.3. Installing it would downgrade the libraries every other pipeline depends on, so it was left out.
openItems.recommendation: Run the marketing-mix profile as a separate ML service (ML_MMM_SERVICE_URL) with its own environment.

openItems.observation: Anomaly detection, segmentation, Chronos forecasting and incrementality run and persist results, but are not counted as "active routes": their evaluations report no metrics to qualify against, or they register no deployable artifact.
openItems.recommendation: Decide what evidence should qualify these tasks, then add it to their results.

openItems.area: Pages with no local data source
openItems.observation: Boards (no card-creation API), ChatGPT Ads, signal deliveries on AdSync/Delivery, connector data on Integrations. Loopback webhook destinations are deliberately blocked by the egress policy, so local delivery cannot be simulated honestly.
openItems.recommendation: Connect real test destinations; these pages then fill from real deliveries.

openItems.observation: Still a single 23 MB JSON document. Reads are now cheap; each write still rewrites the whole document (p95 request time about 1 s).
openItems.recommendation: Move the large event histories (WhatsApp, call, recent events, personalization) into their own tables.

openItems.observation: Ad-platform delivery, CRM writeback, outbound WhatsApp and calls, calendar sync, report e-mail, Stripe billing and file storage are marked Blocked per feature.
openItems.recommendation: Connect provider test accounts, then re-run npm run live:verify:features.
